name: Campo Trailhead
description: The southern terminus sits in dry chaparral beside the US-Mexico border monument. Morning wind moves through sage and chain-link; a distant highway hums. Sparrows tick in the brush as packed dirt takes the first footsteps of a walk toward Canada.

name: Exiting Mount Laguna
description: The morning breeze is freezing cold. Yesterday's snowstorm forced me into an early zero day in Mount Laguna.

name: Foster Point - ?
description: Wind whips on this desert lookout point. Nothing but vast expanse all around.

name: Kwaaymii Point - ?
description: Walking along a high ridgeline overlooking Anza Borrego State Park. A day hiker walks by and offers candy bars -- my first trail magic!

name: Anza Borrego State Park
description: Morning birds around 9am

name: 10 mi before scissors crossing
description: The wind is incessant. Low-lying brush shakes, a dried out tree creaks.

name: ~mi 83
description: Save for an occasional butterfly floating by, the desert heat is as oppressive as it is silent -- nothing stirs. Even the sound of my footsteps doesn't carry very far out here.

name: mi 97.5
description: At first glance, the desert appears to be devoid of any living things. Stop long enough to listen, and it comes to life.

name: before san ysidro creek, after montezuma road
description: The low brush and scorching heat of the desert give way to pastures, rolling green hills, and giant oak trees. The breeze and sudden change of scenery are welcome after days of oppressive heat.

name: San Ysidro Creek
description: A symphony of frogs sings all night while the water rushes past. It's a welcome change to the stillness of the last few nights.

name: ~ mi 117
description: It's golden hour. I'm in the shade of a giant oak tree, enjoying a moment of peace as a morning dove coos nearby. I'm grateful to be clean again, thanks to an outdoor shower and a laundry bucket at the Warner Springs Community Center earlier today.

name: San Jacinto foothills
description: A refreshingly chilly morning as I begin the ascent towards San Jacinto. The desert scrub soon begins to change into high alpine forests and burn scars. For now, a low-lying cloud provides respite from the heat, but warns of an impending storm -- a storm that ultimately forces me to seek shelter in town until it passes.

name: San Jacinto State Park
description: I cross long snowfields on the ascent up to San Jacinto peak. While the trail is obscured, the bootpack (usually) guides me in the right direction.

name: Ascent to San Jacinto Peak
description: A breeze through the Jeffrey pines kicks up the smell of butterscotch as chickadees sing. San Jacinto peak offers incredible views of the Inland Empire and Coachella Valley. Looking out from this high up, it's hard to imagine the scorching heat of the desert floor just days ago.

name: San Jacinto SP
description: Wind blows steadily over the ridgeline, but I'm sheltered by a cluster of boulders and pines. I can still see the hazy desert floor far below.

name: San Jacinto SP, past fuller ridge
description: A crisp morning following a cold night. I begin the long descent back down to the desert floor.

name: Cabazon Wind Farm
description: Wind whips through the brush and the power lines. Dozens of wind turbines spin furiously as they tower over me.

name: Dry camp somewhere ~1 mi after Arrastre Trail camp
description: The birds wake up first; soon, other hikers begin to stir, while the true early birds are already hiking past.

name: Somewhere leaving Big Bear.
description: Leaving the town of Big Bear Lake, I tread carefully over numerous scree fields.

name: Day 2 out of big bear
description: Clouds roll in; an afternoon sprinkle catches me in an exposed area. Back at lower elevation, the alpine forest gives way to scraggly manzanitas and succulents.

name: Holcomb Creek
description: Young willow trees grow all along the water's edge. I stop for a refill.

name: Deep Creek Bridge
description: I stand on a bridge overlooking Deep Creek a few hundred feet below, deliberating whether to continue on or take a detour to the Cedar Glen Malt Shop. Onion rings win this time.

name: Deep Creek - ???
description: A solitary campsite near the water. Resting up for another side quest tomorrow: Deep Creek Hot Springs.

name: Mojave River Forks Reservoir
description: Last night's rainstorm continues through the morning. Everything is wet, but inside the tent I am warm and dry.

name: Approaching Cajon Pass
description: Powerlines overhead remind me that I'm getting closer to civilization. The infamous McDonald's stop is near.

name: Angeles National Forest
description: Unable to get to a water source before sundown, I dry camp on the descent from Mt. Baden-Powell. Morning wind wakes me and the birds.

name: Angeles National Forest
description: Camping on a blustery ridge. I cook dinner and quickly retreat to the tent as the temperature drops. Every guyline I have is pinned to the ground.

name: Upper Shake Campground
description: Tonight's campsite is straight out of a post-apocalyptic film. Ravaged by fire years ago, now completely overgrown, it's equally peaceful and disturbing.

name: Tehachapi Wind Farm
description: Surrounded by giants. Wind turbines spin wildly as far as the eye can see.

name: Leaving Tehachapi
description: One of the toughest climbs yet -- my pack is filled to the brim with food and water leaving Tehachapi.

name: South Sierra
description: Momentarily in a lush forest, I have no idea what awaits me -- the next day I drop back into the scorching desert for one of the trail's longest water carries.

name: South Sierra
description: The scenery hints at the beginnings of the Sierra -- trees grow taller, the wind blows cooler. One last stretch of desert, then it's all mountains.

name: South Sierra
description: Afternoon snack break and a quick water refill. Clear skies, warm sun, and some very vocal bugs hiding in the grass.

name: Horseshoe Meadow
description: An evening thunderstorm rolls in just as I descend from Trail Pass. Sounds like a good time to get into town.

name: Chicken Spring Lake
description: Nighttime by the lake. It's freezing outside, but the tent is warm. I'm beat after climbing back up the pass with a fresh resupply weighing me down, but the frogs keep me awake.

name: South Sierra; SEKI National Park
description: A short rest to dry off following a deep river crossing. I'm surrounded by lush grass, but see the snowy caps peeking out from behind the pines. Birdsong bounces off the steep granite walls.

name: Crabtree Meadows
description: After a midnight wakeup and sunrise summit of Mt. Whitney, the descent back to Crabtree Meadows is nothing short of grueling. A quick pause by the river to fill up water before trudging on.

name: Ascent to Forester Pass
description: Beginning the ascent to Forester Pass before sunrise, the world is frozen. Puddles thaw and crunch underfoot as the sun peeks over the horizon.

name: Bubbs Creek
description: Town day! A relatively quick climb over Kearsarge Pass, and then it's a well-deserved rest in Bishop.

name: South of Kearsarge Pass
description: Cicadas in the trees -- for now, I'm surrounded by them, but in a few miles I'll be well above the treeline and hear nothing but wind.

name: Bullfrog Lake
description: The sun warms my skin as a cool breeze blows. Small waves lap up against the lake's edge as I pause for a snack, taking in the granite peaks that surround me.

name: Rae Lakes
description: Coming down from snowy Glen Pass, I'm greeted by a stunning sunset over a chain of crystal clear lakes. Wildflowers and lush grasses line their banks.

name: Woods Creek, Kings Canyon National Park
description: Another beautiful, cloudless day in the Sierra. A river runs through the canyon below.

name: Kings Canyon National Park (need to confirm)
description: A steady breeze blows through the canyon, rustling a grove of poplar trees near the trail.

name: Kings Canyon National Park (need to confirm)
description: Branches sway, leaves flutter -- poplar trees dance in the wind.

name: John Muir Wilderness - Ascent to Selden Pass
description: Groves of trees amidst rocky outcroppings, I make my way up toward Selden Pass. An entire valley comes into view as I ascend.

name: Ascent to Silver Pass
description: A waterfall cascades down granite boulders, while a refreshing mist settles on my face.

name: Cicadas right before Mammoth
description: Cicadas chirp overhead, flies buzz around me as I eat my last snack. I'm just a few short miles away from my next resupply, Mammoth Lakes, so the trail is more crowded than it's been over the last few days.

name: Soda Springs - Tuolumne Meadows
description: A cold spring bubbles beneath me. As I lean down to inspect it, I notice tiny carbonation bubbles rising through the water.

name: Yosemite National Park
description: Long, exposed meadows in between patches of mosquito-ridden forest. I can't stop for long or I'll get eaten alive.

name: Stanislaus National Forest
description: After an unexpected overnight stopover in Kennedy Meadows North, I continue on through endless fields of wildflowers -- some of them grow taller than my head.

name: Stanislaus National Forest
description: One of my favorite bird calls of the Sierra Nevada -- the XXX?? What is this bird?

name: Ascent to Ebbetts Pass
description: A cloudless day rapidly turns to hail and thunderstorms over the pass. Cold hail lands in a warm pond and appears to be bubbling -- I'm witnessing a rare phenomenon known as thermal effervescence.

name: I think humbold-toiyabe national forest but idk
description: After waiting out the worst of the storm, I crest the pass and continue on in the rain. Spirits are low until I stumble upon a bike race, and I'm welcomed over to their basecamp with hot ramen -- the best possible trail magic for a cold, wet day.

name: Lake Aloha - Desolation Wilderness
description: A serene moment at the water's edge: the late afternoon sun glistens against the lake; snowy granite peaks surround me.

name: Granite Chief Wilderness
description: Passing over the backs of ski resorts, the trail follows a windy ridge. Vast valleys sprawl out on either side, and I catch glimpses of Lake Tahoe.

name: Alpine Meadows Ski Resort
description: Steady wind rustles poplar leaves.

name: Palisades Ski Resort
description: The winds pick up at night, but my campsite is protected. Ski lifts sway in the distance.

name: Hat Creek Rim
description: A sunny day turns to night as dark clouds roll in, releasing thunder, lightning, and golf ball-sized hail. This section of trail is very exposed, so I pause near a cluster of trees to let the storm pass.

name: Burney Falls State Park
description: Ospreys circle overhead and echo through the tall trees. I'm back on trail after a quick detour to see the majestic Burney Falls.

name: Ridge overlooking Mt. Shasta
description: Tree trunks here are drooping with moss. Tonight's campsite is a ridge overlooking Mt. Shasta, but I have to hack my way through the undergrowth first.

name: High voltage power lines overhead
description: I exit the dense forest for just a moment to pass under high voltage power lines.

name: South of Mt. Shasta
description: The forest comes alive in the mornings. A deer wanders onto the trail, mere feet away from me.

name: Deer Creek - Shasta-Trinity National Forest
description: A water crossing in the most magical, fairyland forest. Lush green all around me, ferns peek out of every rock crevasse and massive leaves blanket the ground.

name: Centipede Gulch Trail - Shasta-Trinity National Forest
description: A small creek is a reminder of the tiny beauty around me -- morning light filters through the dense canopy, illuminating a group of yellowjackets at the water; a mushroom grows atop a tree trunk; a perfect spiderweb is seemingly suspended in mid-air.

name: Shasta Trinity NF
description: I walk down an exposed ridge, the sun suprisingly hot today. Large bugs hide in the bushes and jump in front of me as I walk by.

name: Before Hwy 3
description: There must have been rain recently, though today's heat and blue skies show no indication that it ever happened. I quicken my pace -- town is near, and a home cooked meal from a kind trail angel awaits.

name: Near the California-Oregon Border
description: Last night, I officially crossed the Oregon border! Today, I'm greeted by bees in the wildflowers, hemlock forests, and sweeping vistas across multi colored landscapes.

name: TBD title
description: Stumbled upon a cooler full of sodas today -- more trail magic!

name: Before Ashland
description: Stopped in a grove of poplar trees. Multi-colored wildflowers grow tall alongside the trail.

name: Right before Hwy 140
description: Huge rock slides create sections of volcanic scree which slows my travel. I roll into camp at exactly 30 miles for the day, hoping for soft dirt tomorrow.

name: Sky Lakes Wilderness
description: The dirt is red and yellow, the air is crisp and cool. Birds chatter excitedly, and ripe huckleberries are everywhere. Little did I know that this would be my final day on trail.

name: Christi's Spring - Sky Lakes Wilderness
description: Only crickets keep me company tonight. Earlier this afternoon, my foot pain dramatically increased, and I made the difficult decision to turn around hike 12 miles back to Hwy 140. This would be my final night on trail.
